advisory.finding: The test still carries @pytest.mark.requires_posix_named_semaphore, but the new harness only uses ctx.Pipe and ctx.Process and creates no SemLock. Unless the code under test itself uses multiprocessing semaphores, the marker no longer describes a real need. The test would be skipped, and counted as a sandbox-compatibility skip, on hosts that deny semaphores even though it could run there.
scenarios: A host that denies sem_open but allows pipes and spawn skips this race test needlessly, which hides regressions in same-ticket publication atomicity.

pyproject.toml:766-767: `timeout = 300` / `timeout_method = "thread"`; with this method pytest-timeout dumps stacks and hard-exits the process when time runs out
dropped.finding: recv() and join() have no timeout, so a hung or deadlocked worker is only stopped by pytest-timeout. With timeout_method="thread", pytest-timeout ends the whole pytest process (or xdist worker) instead of failing just this test, and it leaves the two non-daemon children running as orphans. The old future.result(timeout=60) failed only this test, so a hang now has a wider blast radius.
scenarios: A real regression makes the two publishers deadlock on a tracker lock: the whole session or xdist worker aborts at 300 s, and the other tests' results and the sandbox counted-skip accounting are lost.
When the run aborts, the spawned workers can keep holding git/tracker locks in tmp repos.
dropped.suggested_fix: In _race_two_commit_workers, before each recv() call `if not recv.poll(240): pytest.fail("commit worker did not report within 240 s")`. In the finally block, call worker.join(timeout=10) and then worker.terminate() on any worker that is still alive, so a hang fails just this test and no orphans are left.
